cells.tense: The picturing is done and it's resting here, and you're the one who carried it the whole way.
cells.ask: Add one more true piece to what you've already made, then set it down for the rest of today.
cells.core:
What you hoped for, you went and felt your way into until it was yours. This is the good shape of it, and you're standing in it: the pull holds steady, the work comes back to you on its own, and you return to it without having to talk yourself into it. Coming back again and again is what made it solid, not the size of the idea. The calm inside is earned.

Let this finished thing feed what comes next. One more true piece added today, and then stop. That gives you a forward motion you don't have to shove.
cells.sheetLine: What you pictured is here, and you're the one who felt it into being.
cells.verb: feeling a vision all the way through until it's real
cells.place: under a pull you didn't invent and can't argue away

cells.tense: You're already out ahead of this again, holding a finished version that hasn't been lived into yet.
cells.ask: Take one piece of what you're building and work it as it stands for twenty minutes, then put it down.
cells.core:
You can see the version where the picture lands cleanly, and you want to drag today toward it. So the pushing starts early, before there's anything to push against. What you're protecting is real — you don't want the thing to slip — but care with nothing to hold it starts to squeeze, and squeezing is what empties you.

The way back is tending one thing in the shape it actually has right now. Not the whole future. One piece, in front of you, as it is — and a day of that is enough. You'll still be tending it. It just won't leave you scraped out.
cells.sheetLine: The future you're reaching for can't be lived in. The piece in front of you can.

cells.tense: You turned from a direction you once wanted, and you're still standing at that turn, well past it.
cells.ask: Write down three things you're drawn to right now, without judging which one is correct.
cells.core:
Something you knew you wanted has faded behind you, and you haven't walked toward it in a long while. If you're honest, no pull stands out from the others — they all look the same from where you are. Feelings in a room this quiet won't tell you much, and pushing desire back into the room won't work either.

Thinking does more here than feeling: hold a few possibilities in your head at once and let your own mind sort them before you announce anything. Three names on paper, no verdict. What that gives back is the ability to recognize a direction the next time one shows up.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped being able to tell one pull from another, and the not-knowing has gone quiet.

cells.tense: The pen's been down a while, in a room where your own handwriting covers the walls.
cells.ask: Say one sentence out loud about something you made, and say plainly that you made it.
cells.core:
You're living in a life that has this thing running through it — the pull you followed, the picture you built and got. It's in the room whether or not you bring it up. But the credit for it lands somewhere other than you. Timing, luck, the right break — the work that made it goes quiet, and so do the times you chose to keep at it.

Bring it back to the plainer shape: this came from your hands. Nothing else was doing that. One sentence, spoken once, that says so — that's the whole ask. What it hands back is the record, corrected in your own mouth.
cells.sheetLine: You made this. Right now something else gets the credit.
